description: This line plot illustrates the progression of model accuracy across 19 discrete evaluation points, comparing “Initial Accuracy” (green line with square markers) and “Final Accuracy” (blue line with circular markers), both with error bars indicating variability. The x-axis, labeled with integer values from 1 to 19, represents sequential evaluation steps or iterations, with no explicit unit or scale type specified but appearing linear. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, representing the proportion of correct predictions. The green “Initial Accuracy” line begins at approximately 0.35 at step 1, rises to a peak of ~0.50 at step 5, dips to ~0.30 at step 7, recovers to ~0.52 at step 13, and ends at ~0.42 at step 19, showing moderate fluctuation with generally low to mid-range values. The blue “Final Accuracy” line starts at ~0.65 at step 1, increases to ~0.85 at step 5, dips to ~0.72 at step 7, peaks again at ~0.92 at step 9, drops to ~0.70 at step 11, rises to ~0.90 at step 15, and ends at ~0.90 at step 19, consistently remaining above 0.65 and generally higher than initial accuracy, with larger error bars suggesting greater variability in final performance across evaluations.
